title: Line Reflection
summary: Determine if a line parallel to the y-axis exists such that reflecting all given n points on a 2D plane results in a set of points identical to the original set.
statement: Determine if a line parallel to the y-axis exists such that reflecting all given n points on a 2D plane results in a set of points identical to the original set. Allow for repeated points among the given coordinates.
constraints: 1 <= len(points) <= 10000; each x and y is an integer between -100000000 and 100000000.
Seek a vertical line x=c. Reflections must keep the same y. Compare coordinate sets, so repeated identical points do not need equal multiplicities.
hints: Any valid vertical axis lies halfway between the leftmost and rightmost x coordinates.
Store distinct coordinate pairs and use twice the axis to avoid floating-point arithmetic.
Let s=min_x+max_x. Require (s-x,y) in the set for every (x,y).
Extremes fix the only possible axis; testing every reflected coordinate proves that axis works.
editorial: A reflection exchanges the minimum and maximum x coordinates, fixing twice the axis as their sum. Every distinct (x,y) must have a partner (sum-x,y). Points on the axis partner with themselves. Repeated coordinates do not change the set, and half-integer axes need no floating point. The oracle independently enumerates candidate axes from all pairs.

tests.explanation: The line x=0 exchanges the two points while preserving y=1, so reflection is possible.
The x coordinates are symmetric, but the y coordinates differ. A vertical reflection cannot exchange these points, so the answer is false.
